Clinical details: Driver, head-on RTC at approx. 50 mph, restrained, airbags deployed. Seatbelt bruising across chest and lower abdomen. GCS 15. HR 94, BP 128/80. Trauma call.

Technique: Non-contrast CT head and cervical spine, followed by contrast-enhanced CT chest, abdomen and pelvis (split-bolus arterial/portal venous phase). Multiplanar bone reformats.

Head:
No intracranial haemorrhage or extra-axial collection. No midline shift. No skull vault or skull base fracture. Grey-white differentiation preserved.

Cervical spine:
No acute fracture or malalignment of the cervical spine. Craniocervical junction intact. Prevertebral soft tissues not thickened.

Chest:
No pneumothorax or haemothorax. No pulmonary contusion or laceration. Mediastinum not widened; no mediastinal haematoma and no traumatic aortic injury. No rib, sternal or clavicular fracture.

Abdomen:
No solid organ injury. No free fluid or free gas. No bowel wall thickening or mesenteric haematoma to suggest bowel or mesenteric injury. Kidneys enhance symmetrically; no perinephric haematoma. Adrenals unremarkable.

Pelvis:
Pelvic ring intact. No pelvic haematoma. Bladder unremarkable.

Thoracolumbar spine:
No thoracolumbar spinal fracture. Alignment maintained.

Other:
Subcutaneous fat stranding across the lower anterior abdominal wall corresponding to the seatbelt bruising. No abdominal wall muscle disruption or hernia.

Conclusion:
1. No acute traumatic injury identified.
2. Seatbelt-related subcutaneous contusion of the lower anterior abdominal wall only.

Preliminary findings relayed to the trauma team leader in CT at 14:32.
